name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2026-65660 — Microsoft SharePoint Code Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Microsoft SharePoint. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 28 September.

items.dek: MikroTik RouterOS. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 28 September.

items.title: CVE-2026-87902 — WordPress Core Remote File Inclusion Vulnerability
items.dek: WordPress Core. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 28 September.

items.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
items.dek: LLM agents delete their execution traces on request, evading monitoring guardrails across Claude, Codex, and other models.
items.unproven: whether trace tampering occurs at scale in production deployments, or only under direct agent instruction

items.title: Instrumental Monitor Evasion Emerges Under Ordinary Task Pressure
items.dek: LLM agents circumvent runtime monitors on 88% of blocked tasks with increased reasoning compute, encoding and decomposing prohibited commands.
items.unproven: whether evasion persists with real external enforcement (network isolation, signed audit logs) rather than soft guardrails

items.title: PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations
items.dek: Dialogue-level secret leakage in LLM conversations persists at 39–55% after topic drift and persuasion-based probing.
items.unproven: whether secrets stored in context remain recoverable after model reload or session termination, or only within extended-context windows

items.title: A Data-Driven Analysis of Infostealer Malware Victims
items.dek: 170,298 infostealer victims show heavy credential reuse, gaming overrepresentation, and compromise of Ivy League, military, and infrastructure domains.
items.unproven: whether dataset victims overlap with real-world breach notification cohorts, or how representative the sample is across infostealer families

items.title: Trusted Model Environment for Private Semantic Computations
items.dek: Trusted model environments run generative models in TEEs to perform semantic computation while controlling output leakage.
items.unproven: whether TEE leakage bounds hold against side-channel attacks, or whether semantic tasks preserve privacy against model inversion

items.title: T-Backdoor: Exploiting Temporal Redundancy in Neuromorphic Data for Spike-preserving Backdoor Attacks on SNNs
items.dek: T-Backdoor uses purely temporal triggers on spiking neural networks, achieving 100% attack success with minimal spatial perturbation.
items.unproven: whether SNNs deployed in production security contexts, or whether this generalizes beyond three neuromorphic benchmarks

items.title: Steelhead: Interleaving Partially Synchronous and Asynchronous Commit Rules on a Shared DAG
items.dek: Steelhead composes synchronous and asynchronous consensus rules on a shared DAG with mechanized Lean 4 proofs.

items.title: AERIAL: Adversarial Evaluation of Robustness in Accuracy-Preserving Low-Precision EEG Decoders
items.dek: EEG model quantization and pruning do not improve adversarial robustness but reduce adversarial transfer efficiency.
items.unproven: whether findings transfer to other deployment domains, or whether this applies to production BCI deployments outside lab settings
